AgentHome.description:
Where an agent keeps its own data for a session, as its host resolved
it from the adapter's environment (plan 9d decision 1): `root` is
Claude's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude`, Codex's `CODEX_HOME` or
`~/.codex`; `sqlite_root` is Codex's `CODEX_SQLITE_HOME` if set.
Canonical, its bytes as the filesystem gave them (O11). A host's report
is not verified by the collector beyond its shape (`is_well_formed`).

AnswerRequest.description:
`POST /api/sessions/{id}/pending/{pending_id}/answer` (ACP core §9): an
option for a permission request, or an action for an elicitation, with
the form's content when it accepts.

AnswerResponse.description:
202 to an answer: it is queued for the session's host, and delivered now
or on the host's next connection (ACP core §4.6). The verdict follows on
the session stream as `pending_changed`.

request_id.description: Carried by the host's `answer_result` for this answer.

session_id.description:
Set when the error leaves a session reachable by id (e.g. a session
start whose delivery is unknown: the session was created and may
still start, but the caller has no other way to learn its id).

AttachedSession.description: A session that a host still has an adapter for, reported in `hello`.

AttachmentUsage.description:
`GET /api/settings/attachments` (plan 6a): the owner's attachment store,
for Settings (ACP core §15, maintainer decision 6a).

count.description: Stored images, each counted once however often it was sent.

AuthSessionItem.description:
One entry of `GET /api/auth/sessions` (kernel spec §3.2): a signed-in
device, most recently used first.

current.description: The session this request came with.

id.description:
What `DELETE /api/auth/sessions/{id}` takes: the SHA-256 of the
session's token, never the token.

CancelResponse.description:
`POST /api/sessions/{id}/cancel`: how the open turn ended. Usually
`cancelled`, but `completed` or `failed` if the turn ended before the
cancel reached the agent, and `interrupted` if the session was parked or
closed while the cancel was outstanding, or its adapter exited.

Capabilities.description:
`hello.capabilities`. Deserialized leniently: a capability this build
does not know (a newer host, a minor protocol bump) is skipped, never a
reason to refuse the whole `hello`. The generated schema still lists
`Capability` as a closed `oneOf` (there is no open-ended JSON Schema
equivalent), but that is a description of the known values, not a
constraint hennery itself enforces: an entry outside it is ignored, not
rejected, so a schema-validating client or proxy must not reject a
`hello` on an unknown capability either.

Capability.description:
A feature a host implements, announced in `hello` (ACP core §3.3). The
collector never sends a frame that needs a capability to a host that
lacks it.

oneOf.description: Project enumeration and browsing.
Image content blocks in prompts.
Explicit park (`park_session`).
Resolving typed paths (`resolve_path`, kernel spec §5.4).

Removing a deleted session's transcript from the agent's own data
(`forget_session`, plan 9d decision 4).

committed.description:
Highest committed seq per session listed in `hello`; the host
fast-forwards its counters if they are lower (lost outbox).

oneOf.description:
Start a new session: spawn the adapter, `session/new`, then apply the
requested config (ACP core §3.3, §4.3). Completed by
`session_started` | `start_failed`.

committed_seq.description:
The collector's highest committed seq for this session; the host
continues from the larger of this and its own counter (§5.1).

oneOf.description:
Attach a parked, closed or failed session again: spawn the adapter and
`session/load` it with replay suppression (ACP core §4.3, §4.5).
Completed by `session_started` | `start_failed`, like a start.

agent_session_id.description:
The adapter's own session id, from the stored `session_started`:
the host keeps no copy across restarts.

committed_seq.description: Fast-forward the host's counter before the first frame (§5.1).

content.description: ACP ContentBlocks, built by the frontend.

oneOf.description:
Stop the turn in flight: `session/cancel` to the adapter. Completed
by that turn's `turn_ended` (ACP core §3.3, §4.4), whatever its
outcome: a turn that finished first is not cancelled.

Switch one config option of an attached session (`session/set_config_option`).
Completed by `config_applied` | `error` (ACP core §3.3).

The operator's choice for a permission request. Completed by
`answer_result` (ACP core §4.6); it has no collector waiter.

The operator's answer to an elicitation; `content` only with
`accept`. Completed by `answer_result`, like a permission's.

Resolve a typed path on the host, where the filesystem is (kernel
spec §5.2, §5.4): absolute, or `~` / `~/…` for the host user's home.
Completed by `resolved_path` | `error{invalid}`.
Completed by `session_parked{operator}` (ACP core §4.8).
Completed by `session_closed` (ACP core §4.8).

Enumerate the git repositories under the host's workspace roots
(ACP core §7). Answered by `projects`; only to a host with the
`projects` capability.

List the subdirectories of `path`, an absolute path inside the host's
browse fence (ACP core §7). Answered by `directory` | `error`; only to
a host with the `projects` capability.

A hat the operator purged (kernel spec §5.5; plan 9c decisions 10
and 12, A7): sent after every reconciled handshake, one per purged
hat, for good. The host forgets what it keeps for the hat (its
composed agent home, plan 8): only for an id that is `hat-<hex>`,
and only once no adapter of that hat runs. No answer; a host that
does not know the frame logs and ignores it, so no capability is
needed.

Remove a deleted session's transcript from the agent's own data on
the host (plan 9d decision 4): only to a host with the
`forget_session` capability. The host acts only on an exact match
of its own registry (B1). Answered by `session_forgotten` |
`error{invalid}`.

ConfigValue.description:
The value of one config option (ACP `session/set_config_option`): a
select's value id, or a boolean toggle's state.

CreateHatRequest.description:
`POST /api/hats`: a name, 1 to 64 printable characters, unique in any
case, and a `#rrggbb` colour (slate when absent).

CreateMcpConnectionRequest.description:
`POST /api/mcp/connections` (step-up): 201 with the new
`McpConnectionItem`, `not_connected`, with no credential and no mounts.
Absent: the `Authorization` header with `Bearer `, every tool, a public
upstream. Unknown fields are refused.

Its own codes, beyond every route's (see `McpConnectionItem`): 403
`step_up_required`; 400 `invalid` (a field refused, `message` says
which, or a hat that is not the owner's); 400 `unsupported_cred_kind`
(an OAuth kind, until plan 8f); 409 `slug_taken` (another of the owner's
connections has the slug); 409 `too_many_connections` (at most 256 per
owner).

hat_id.description: One of the owner's hats; fixed once created.

internal_network.description: Absent: `false`. The upstream is on the operator's own network.

label.description:
1 to 64 bytes of UTF-8 once trimmed (stored trimmed), with no
control or invisible format character.

slug.description: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}$`, unique per owner; fixed once created.

static_header.description:
Absent: `Authorization`. An HTTP header name of at most 64 bytes,
not one the gateway sets or filters itself (`host`, `content-type`,
`cookie`, `mcp-session-id`, `proxy-*`, `sec-*` and the like).

static_prefix.description:
Absent: `Bearer `. At most 32 visible ASCII characters or spaces;
`""` for none.

tool_allowlist.description:
Absent or `null`: every tool. Else at most 1024 names, each 1 to 128
visible ASCII characters; duplicates are dropped, the order kept.

url.description:
Absolute `https`, or `http` only with `internal_network`; with a
host, without a user name, password or fragment; at most 2048 bytes.
A query is kept, but a secret belongs in the credential.

DirEntry.description: One subdirectory in a `browse_directory` answer (ACP core §7).

git.description: It holds `.git`: a repository, or a worktree of one.

name.description: The entry's file name, not a path.

DirectoryListing.description:
`GET /api/hosts/{id}/browse?path=` (ACP core §7, §9): the
subdirectories of a directory on the host.

parent.description: Its parent, if browsing it is allowed too.

ElicitationAction.description: The operator's answer to an elicitation (ACP `elicitation/create`).

EnrollRequest.description:
`POST /api/hosts/enroll` (kernel spec §4.1): a host pairs itself with a
code and the public half of the key it generated.

EnrollResponse.description: 201 to an enrollment: the id the host names itself by in `hello`.

EventDto.description: One stored timeline event, as served by REST and SSE.

ForgetKind.description:
What a forget names on the host (plan 9d decision 4, B2): a kind of
entry, never a path. The masked path each stands for is `masked`.

oneOf.description:
The whole forget, when it could not start (no home, an unknown id,
an agent this host cannot forget for yet).
The transcript and its family in each project directory (B9).
Codex's own database copies of the conversation (plan 9d-ii).

ForgetOutcome.description:
How a forget ended (plan 9d decision 4): `complete` when the check
afterwards found nothing named left (B4).

ForgetReason.description:
Why something named was not removed: a fixed code the host chooses
(plan 9d B2), never free text.

oneOf.description: A live actor on the host has that agent session id (decision 13, B7).

Another forget of the same agent session is running on the host
(B7; the review's item 3).
This host cannot forget for that agent (yet).
The session recorded no agent home (decision 11).
The host's registry has no such (agent, id, home) (B1).
Another kept session refers to the same agent session (B8).

The root failed a check: `/`, `$HOME` or an ancestor, the host's data
directory, not canonical, not the host user's, writable by others.
The root is not there (any more).
A symlink, reported and never followed or removed (decision 8).
A kind directory that is not a real directory.
A kind directory not the host user's, or writable by others (B3).
The walk reached another file system (R2).
The walk reached its depth bound (R2).
The forget's deadline passed before the removal was done (B6).
Still there after the removal (B4).
The removal failed midway (B3).

The collector's own: the host answered `error{invalid}` for the id
(decision 8, O10).

The collector's own: the host was revoked and never connects again
(O10).

ForgetRemaining.description:
Something a forget left (plan 9d decision 4). `retry: false` marks what
a retry cannot change.

ForgetWhat.description: One kind of entry and how many of them (plan 9d B2).

HatItem.description:
One hat (kernel spec §5.1): an entry of `GET /api/hats`, and the answer
to its creation and its changes.

default_for_new_hosts.description: The hat newly paired hosts get as their default.

purging.description:
A purge of it began and has not finished (plan 9c A12): it is
frozen, so nothing starts, resumes or moves in or out of it, and a
`POST /api/hats/{id}/purge` again resumes the purge.

HatResolution.description:
200 to `POST /api/hats/resolve`: the canonical path, whether it exists
and is a directory there, and its hat, with the rule that decided it
(absent: the host's default hat).

HatResolveRequest.description:
`POST /api/hats/resolve` (kernel spec §8): which hat `path` resolves to
on `host_id`, as a session started there would get. The host resolves
the path; `~` and `~/…` are its user's home.

capabilities.description:
What this host implements (ACP core §3.3). `Capability` lists
the values this version knows; an unknown one is ignored, not
rejected (see `Capabilities`). Absent means none.

proof.description:
Proof of possession of the host's key (ACP core §3.5): its
Ed25519 signature, hex, over `hello_proof_message(nonce, host_id,
protocol_version)`, where the nonce is the one the collector sent
in the upgrade response's `hennery-hello-nonce` header.

workspace_roots.description:
The workspace roots from the host's config (ACP core §7), as
configured. Absent means none (an older host).

oneOf.description:
Every state-bearing fact is a sequenced frame: it goes through the host
outbox and is acked (ACP core §3.3).

A rejected request. Not outboxed: a rejection means nothing happened,
so losing it only costs the collector a timeout.

The answer to `resolve_path` (kernel spec §5.4). Not outboxed: a
probe changes nothing, so a lost answer costs only a retry.
`canonical` is absolute, symlinks resolved, with no `.`, `..` or
trailing slash; for a path that does not exist, its deepest existing
ancestor is resolved and the rest normalised by its text.

Sent once per connection after the unacked outbox has been resent.
The collector reconciles `hello.attached_sessions` only after this
frame, so a resent `turn_ended` is never duplicated by a synthesised
one (ACP core §5.2).

The answer to `list_projects` (ACP core §3.3, §7): the git
repositories under the workspace roots. A probe reply: not outboxed,
it answers only the connection it was asked on.

home.description:
The host user's home directory, canonical, so the picker can
expand `~` (frontend §7). Absent if the host has none.

partial.description: A bound cut the enumeration short: there may be more.

oneOf.description:
The answer to `forget_session` (plan 9d decision 4): what was
removed and what is left, as kinds and counts (B2). Like a probe's
reply it is not outboxed and answers only the connection it was
asked on: a forget is idempotent, so a lost answer costs a retry.

The answer to `browse_directory` (ACP core §3.3, §7): the
subdirectories of `path`. A probe reply, like `projects`.

parent.description: Its parent, canonical, if browsing it is allowed too.

HostItem.description:
One entry of `GET /api/hosts` (kernel spec §8): a paired host, revoked
ones included.

connected.description: Connected and reconciled: requests reach it now.

default_hat_id.description: The hat of its sessions that no path rule claims (kernel spec §5.1).

workspace_roots.description:
From its latest reconciled connection, as configured on the host
(ACP core §7): where its projects are, and where browsing may start.

HostProjects.description:
`GET /api/hosts/{id}/projects?path=` (ACP core §7, §9): the recent
projects of one hat, and the git repositories under the host's
workspace roots.

home.description: The host user's home directory, for expanding `~` (frontend §7).

partial.description: The host cut its enumeration short: there may be more.

recents.description: Newest first: only those whose path resolves to that hat now.

recents_hat_id.description:
The hat `recents` belong to: the one `path` resolves to on the host,
or the host's default hat without one (kernel spec §5.3).

HostRemovalState.description: Whether a host removal is still retried (plan 9d decision 6, O10).

oneOf.description: Retried at the host's next handshake.

Done with something left that no retry changes: listed until it is
dismissed.

Indexed.description:
Fields the collector may read from a session event. Closed set (ACP core §3.2).

The catalogue extracts (`config_options`, `current_model`,
`current_mode`, `current_axes`) travel together: when `config_options`
is present and not empty, the four are one snapshot of the adapter's
config. An absent or empty `config_options` means "no read-back", never
"the adapter has no config" (a response that failed to parse looks
empty).

commands.description:
On an `available_commands_update`: the adapter's slash commands, the
full list (ACP `AvailableCommand` objects, those hennery can parse).
An empty list means the adapter has none, unlike an empty
`config_options`. Never part of the catalogue snapshot.

config_options.description:
The full config catalogue: the adapter's ACP `SessionConfigOption`
objects, for the UI. The collector stores it and never reads it.

current_axes.description: The current value of every other option, by config id.

current_mode.description: The current value of the mode option.

current_model.description: The current value of the model option.

early.description:
On an update the adapter sent before the session was announced:
replayed by `session/load`, or sent while the start ran (ACP core
§4.5). What it says may be older than what the collector holds, so
its title only fills an empty one (plan 6b decision 2).

pending.description: On `pending_opened`: the request's id, kind, option ids and title.

title.description:
On a `session_info_update` that names a title: the title the agent
reported, as it sent it; empty when it cleared it (ACP `null`). The
collector normalises and caps it for the session list.

LifecycleResponse.description:
Result of a park or close: the session's lifecycle once the request took
effect (`parked` or `closed`).

LoginRequest.description:
`POST /api/auth/login` (kernel spec §3.2): the owner's password. 204 and
the session cookie on success. `Debug` leaves the password out.

McpConnectionItem.description:
One MCP gateway connection (gateway spec §2, §9): an entry of
`GET /api/mcp/connections` (200, an array, oldest first), and the answer
to `POST` (201), `PATCH` (200) and `PUT …/{id}/mounts` (200). Never its
secret: `has_credential` says whether one is stored.

Every `/api/mcp/*` route is the operator's and answers
`Cache-Control: no-store`. An error is an `ApiError`; the codes every
route may answer:
- 401 `unauthenticated`: no live session: sign in.
- 403 `setup_required`, `origin_mismatch` or `cross_site`: the browser
  rules refused the request (kernel spec §3.2).
- 415 `unsupported_media_type`: a body that is not `application/json`.
- 400 `invalid_body`: a body that is not JSON; 422 `invalid_body`: one
  that is not the route's shape, an unknown field included. The body is
  never quoted back.
- 413 `body_too_large`: a body over 256 KiB.
- 405, with no body: a method the path does not take.
- 500 `internal`.

Each request type names the codes of its own route. A 403
`step_up_required` asks for a password or passkey check
(`POST /api/auth/step-up/…`); retry after it.

`DELETE /api/mcp/connections/{id}` (step-up) takes no body: 204, its
mounts and credential deleted with it; 403 `step_up_required`, 404
`not_found`.

account_label.description:
The upstream account it is signed in as, when the probe (plan 8f)
learns it; absent otherwise.

cred_kind.description: How it authenticates to its upstream.

has_credential.description: Whether a credential is stored. No route answers the credential.

hat_id.description:
The hat whose sessions may use it. Fixed once created: a grant stays
in its hat.

id.description: `conn-` and 16 hexadecimal digits: the `{id}` of the routes.

internal_network.description:
The upstream is on the operator's own network: its URL may be
`http`, and its requests may reach internal addresses; plain `http`
goes only to an internal address (plans 8b and 8b-ii).

label.description:
The operator's name for it: 1 to 64 bytes of UTF-8 once trimmed
(stored trimmed), with no control or invisible format character.

mounts.description: The hosts it is mounted on, by id, sorted; revoked hosts are left out.

slug.description:
`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}$`, unique per owner; fixed once created.
Agents see the server as `hennery-<slug>`.

static_header.description: The header a `static` token is sent in (by default `Authorization`).

static_prefix.description:
What goes before the token in that header (by default `Bearer `);
may be empty.

status_at.description: When `status` last changed: RFC 3339, as the other stamps.

status_note.description:
Why `status` is what it is, when the probe (plan 8f) says; absent
otherwise.

tool_allowlist.description:
The tools an agent may call: `null`, every tool; `[]`, none; else
these names, in order, without duplicates.

updated_at.description:
When a `PATCH` last changed it: RFC 3339. Mounts and the credential
do not move it.

url.description:
The upstream MCP endpoint, as stored (parsed and serialised). Only
the API's answers show it whole: logs and errors show only its origin.

McpConnectionStatus.description:
A connection's health (gateway spec §7): `not_connected`, not checked
yet; `ok`; `needs_auth`, the operator must sign in again; `error`, with
`status_note`. Plan 8a only ever reports `not_connected`; the probe
(plan 8f) sets the others.

oneOf.description:
Not checked yet: since it was created, or since another origin or
kind deleted its credential.
The last check reached the upstream with its credential.
The upstream wants the operator to sign in again.
The last check failed; `status_note` says how.

McpCredKind.description:
How an MCP gateway connection authenticates to its upstream (gateway
spec §2): `none`; `static`, a token the operator sets; `oauth_dcr` and
`oauth_client`, OAuth (plan 8f). Plan 8a takes `none` and `static`;
naming an OAuth kind in a create or a change answers 400
`unsupported_cred_kind` until plan 8f.

oneOf.description: No credential: the gateway sends the agents' requests as they are.

A token the operator sets (`PUT /api/mcp/connections/{id}/credential`),
sent as `<static_header>: <static_prefix><token>`.
OAuth, the client registered dynamically (plan 8f).
OAuth, with a client the operator registered with the vendor (plan 8f).

McpCredentialRequest.description:
`PUT /api/mcp/connections/{id}/credential` (step-up): a static token,
write-only: 204, the token sealed and stored, replacing any before it.
No route reads it back or clears it; changing the kind or the origin,
or deleting the connection, deletes it. Its `Debug` never shows the
token.

Its own codes, beyond every route's (see `McpConnectionItem`): 403
`step_up_required`; 404 `not_found`; 409 `wrong_cred_kind` (the
connection is not `static`); 400 `invalid` (the token is not 1 to 8192
visible ASCII characters without spaces; never quoted).

token.description: The token, as the upstream takes it after `static_prefix`.

McpMountsRequest.description:
`PUT /api/mcp/connections/{id}/mounts`: the whole set of hosts the
connection is mounted on, replacing the one before, never a delta
(gateway spec §9). No step-up: a mount reaches only a host the owner
paired. 200 with the `McpConnectionItem`.

Its own codes, beyond every route's (see `McpConnectionItem`): 404
`not_found`; 400 `invalid` (a host that is not one of the owner's
paired, unrevoked hosts; more than 1024 hosts; an id over 64 bytes,
which is not quoted back). The limits count the ids as sent, and are
checked before the connection is looked up. A refused set changes
nothing.

host_ids.description: Host ids; `[]` unmounts it everywhere. A repeated id counts once.

OpenTurn.description: A session's open turn, for the detail view.

state.description: `sent` (not yet acknowledged by the adapter) or `started`.

PairingCodeResponse.description:
201 to `POST /api/hosts/pairing-codes` (kernel spec §4.1): a single-use
code for `hennery host join`, shown once.

ParkReason.description: Why a session was parked (ACP core §3.2).

PasskeyCeremony.description:
200 to the start of every passkey ceremony: registration, login and
step-up. `options` is WebAuthn's JSON, for
`navigator.credentials.create()` (registration) or `.get()` (login,
step-up): its `publicKey` goes through
`PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON` or
`parseRequestOptionsFromJSON`. The finish names `ceremony_id`.

PasskeyFinishRequest.description:
The finish of every passkey ceremony: the credential the browser
returned, as `PublicKeyCredential.toJSON()` gives it. `Debug` leaves
the credential out.

PasskeyItem.description:
One of the owner's passkeys: an entry of `GET /api/auth/passkeys`, and
201 to a registration's finish.

PasskeyRegisterRequest.description:
`POST /api/auth/passkeys/register/start` (kernel spec §3.2, plan 3c):
the new passkey's label, 1 to 64 characters.

PathRuleInput.description: One rule of `PUT /api/hosts/{id}/path-rules`, as the operator typed it.

PathRuleItem.description:
One path rule of a host (kernel spec §5.1, §5.2): sessions whose
canonical cwd is `prefix` or under it, by whole segments, belong to
`hat_id`, unless a longer rule covers them too.

prefix.description: Canonical: absolute, no `.` or `..`, no trailing slash.

verified.description:
The host resolved the prefix when the rule was saved; an unverified
rule is the path as typed, normalised by its text alone.

PathRulesRequest.description:
`PUT /api/hosts/{id}/path-rules` (kernel spec §8): the host's whole set
of rules, replacing the one before. The answer is the stored set,
longest prefix first.

PendingExtract.description:
The `pending` extract (ACP core §3.2): what the collector needs to hold
a pending request and validate its answer, without reading the payload.

option_ids.description:
The permission's option ids. Absent for an elicitation, and for a
permission request whose options hennery could not parse.

title.description:
What the question is about, as the agent put it: a permission's tool
call title, an elicitation's message (plan 10b). A push shows it
only under a hat with `details` (kernel spec §6).

PendingItem.description:
One pending request, as the collector holds it: an entry of
`SessionDetail.pending`, and the data of SSE `pending_changed`.

answered.description: An answer has been accepted for it (at most one is).

delivered.description:
The host's verdict on that answer, once one arrived. `true` sticks
(umbrella §6.8): a card shows "answered" only then.

option_ids.description: A permission's option ids: the only valid answers.

turn_id.description: The turn it was asked in.

PendingKind.description: What a pending request asks the operator (ACP core §4.6).

oneOf.description: `session/request_permission`: pick one of the offered options.
`elicitation/create`: fill in a form, or decline.

PendingReason.description: Why a pending request was cancelled (ACP core §4.6).

oneOf.description: The adapter withdrew its own question (`$/cancel_request`).

The operator revoked the session's host (kernel spec §4.3): it will
never connect again to deliver an answer.

PendingResolution.description: How a pending request ended (ACP core §3.2).

oneOf.description: The operator's answer reached the waiting adapter.
The adapter was told the question is off (see `PendingReason`).

PendingState.description:
Where a pending request stands (ACP core §4.6): `open`, then
`delivered` or `cancelled`.

Project.description:
One git repository `list_projects` found under a workspace root (ACP
core §7).

path.description: Absolute and canonical (symlinks resolved), as the host sees it.

PurgePreview.description:
`GET /api/hats/{id}/purge` (kernel spec §5.5; plan 9c decision 11, A13):
what a purge of the hat would delete, read only. Tombstones are not
counted.

purging.description: A purge began and has not finished: a purge resumes it.

recents.description: The project recents of the hat, on every host.

rules.description: The path rules that name the hat, on every host.

running.description:
Those `starting` or `active` on a host the collector reaches: a
purge is refused (409 `sessions_running`) until they are closed.

sessions.description: The hat's sessions, in every lifecycle and on every host.

unassigned.description:
The sessions of no hat (from before hats, when no default hat could
be found), the newest first and at most 100: a purge never deletes
them, so they are listed for the operator to look at (plan 5c).

unassigned_count.description: How many sessions of no hat there are in all.

PurgeResult.description:
200 to `POST /api/hats/{id}/purge` (plan 9c decision 10, A13): what
this purge deleted. A purge that resumes one that stopped counts only
what it deleted itself.

unconfirmed.description:
Sessions closed here, collector-side, while their host may still run
them (presumed parked, or starting or active on a host away): that
host closes them when it is back.

PushKeys.description:
A subscription's keys, as `PushSubscription.toJSON()` gives them
(base64url).

PushPayload.description:
What a push carries to the browser's service worker (kernel spec §6;
plan 10b-ii), encrypted to the browser (RFC 8291): the push service sees
its size only, and that is padded. The service worker shows `title` and
`body` as text, tags the notification `tag`, and on a click opens `url`,
a path of this origin.

url.description: `/sessions/<id>`, or `/mcp`: always a path, never a URL.

PushPolicyItem.description:
One hat's push policy: an entry of `GET /api/push/policies`, one per hat,
oldest hat first, and the answer to `PUT /api/push/policies/{hat_id}`.

PushPolicyRequest.description:
A hat's push policy (kernel spec §6): the body of
`PUT /api/push/policies/{hat_id}`.

generic_title.description: "Session needs your answer", without the session title.

muted.description: No notification for the hat's sessions.

PushRotateRequest.description:
`POST /api/push/subscriptions/rotate`: the push service replaced this
browser's subscription, and its service worker reports the new one
(`pushsubscriptionchange`). No step-up: there is no page to ask on. Only
a subscription whose `old_endpoint` the owner has is replaced, keeping its
id and the session that made it.

PushSubscribeRequest.description:
`POST /api/push/subscriptions` (kernel spec §6, §8): the browser's
`PushSubscription.toJSON()`, and optionally what Settings should list it
as (1 to 64 printable characters; the endpoint's host name when absent).
The endpoint must be `https` on a public domain name at the default
port. Needs a fresh step-up (plan 10a decision 4).

expirationTime.description: Milliseconds since the epoch, as the browser reports it.

PushSubscriptionItem.description:
One push subscription: an entry of `GET /api/push/subscriptions`, and
the answer to `POST` (201 new, 200 the endpoint's earlier one replaced).
The endpoint itself is never shown, only its host.

last_error.description: Why the last delivery failed, when it did.

signed_out.description:
The session that subscribed it has ended or expired: it is no longer
in the signed-in devices, but still receives notifications until it
is removed here.

this_device.description: Subscribed by the session asking: this browser.

PushUnsubscribeRequest.description:
`DELETE /api/push/subscriptions`: this browser unsubscribing, by the
endpoint it knows.

RecentProject.description:
A directory a session started or resumed in on the host (kernel spec
§5.3).

RemovalItem.description:
One kind of entry left on the host, how many, and why (plan 9d B2). Its
path is `kind`'s masked one (`ForgetKind::masked`).

RemovalPending.description: Why a removal is still pending (plan 9d decision 7).

oneOf.description: The host does not announce `forget_session`.
No answer within the wait (30 s).
The host still has the agent's session attached.
Another attempt is running right now.

RemovalState.description:
Where removing the agent's own transcript of a deleted session stands
(plan 9d decision 7).

oneOf.description: Its host removed everything it names.
Something is left (`remaining`), or could not be looked for.
Not done yet (`pending`): retried when the host reconnects.
The session had no agent record: nothing on the host.

SessionBody.description: The body of a sequenced, outboxed session frame.

oneOf.description:
The adapter session exists. Resolves the collector's start waiter.
`indexed` carries the catalogue after the start's config switches
(ACP core §4.3, P-13).

agent_home.description:
Where the agent keeps its data for this session (plan 9d
decision 1), registered on the host before this was sent (B1).
Absent from an older host, for an agent hennery cannot forget
for, or when the host could not resolve or register it.

oneOf.description:
The host accepted a start but could not create the adapter session
(spawn, `initialize` or `session/new` failed). Rejects the start waiter.
The prompt reached the adapter. Resolves the collector's prompt waiter.
An ACP message from the adapter, verbatim in `payload`.

The adapter process is gone and the session is detached (idle reap,
adapter exit, or an operator park). Completes `park_session`.
The operator closed an attached session. Completes `close_session`.

The adapter exited without being asked to (ACP core §2.3). Followed by
`session_parked{adapter_exited}`. The stderr tail is scrubbed.

hennery's own diagnostic that is not state (ACP core §3.2): a failed
re-apply, or update kinds dropped during `session/load` (§4.5).
`note` is a machine code; `text` is scrubbed.

A `set_config` took effect: the catalogue the adapter answered with,
the authoritative read-back (ACP core §3.2). Resolves the collector's
config waiter.

The adapter asked the operator something (ACP core §4.6): its ACP
request verbatim in `payload`, with `indexed.pending`. It waits, with
no timeout, until it is answered or cancelled. Its kind is
`indexed.pending.kind` (the body's own `kind` is its tag).

A pending request is over: answered (`delivered`), or cancelled for
`reason`.

The host's verdict on one answer (umbrella §6.8): `delivered` if the
adapter was still waiting for it. A delivered answer is followed by
`pending_resolved{delivered}`.

The git state of the session's cwd (ACP core §3.2, §7): after the
start and after each turn, when `cwd` is in a work tree and `git`
answered within 3 s (plan 6b-ii decision 11). Never in place of, or
ahead of, the `turn_ended` it follows.

base_commit.description:
On the first state after a new session's start: the commit it
started from. The collector records it once.

branch.description: The branch checked out; absent when detached.

dirty.description: Any staged, unstaged or untracked change.

head.description: The commit checked out; absent on a branch with no commit yet.

worktree.description:
`cwd` is in a linked work tree (`git worktree add`), not the
repository's main one.

SessionCatalog.description:
A session's catalogue: its config options and their current values,
and its slash commands. `GET /api/sessions/{id}/catalog`, the answer to
`POST …/config`, and the data of the SSE `catalog_changed` message (ACP
core §9), always as it stands when sent. Plan and usage join it with
the plans that produce them.

commands.description:
The adapter's slash commands (ACP `AvailableCommand` objects), as
last reported; empty until it reports any (ACP core §7). Always
sent, so the schema and the TypeScript type agree that it is there.

config_options.description: The adapter's ACP `SessionConfigOption` objects, as last reported.

SessionDetail.description:
`GET /api/sessions/{id}` (ACP core §9): the list item, as stored, the
open turn and the pending requests still open.

cwd.description: Canonical on its host since hats (umbrella §8.2).

git_branch.description: The branch checked out in `cwd`, as the host last reported it.

git_dirty.description: Whether `cwd`'s work tree had changes, as the host last reported.

hat_id.description:
The hat the session belongs to (umbrella §8.2), decided at its
start: a hat's id, or empty for a session from before hats whose
host and owner had no default hat to give it.

last_event_at.description:
When its last listed event was written (RFC 3339, UTC, three
fractional digits): the list's sort key, newest first.

model.description: The current model and mode, as the host last reported them.

pending.description: Open pending requests, oldest first: what the operator can answer.

presumed_parked.description:
Parked only because its host has been offline past the threshold
(ACP core §5.3); the host may still be running it.

title.description: The title the agent reported, on one line and capped.

SessionItem.description:
One session as the session list shows it (ACP core §8, §9; frontend
§5), read from `sessions` alone: never the catalogue, commands or plan
(P-23). The detail serves it as stored; the list, `bounded`.

cwd.description: Canonical on its host since hats (umbrella §8.2).

git_branch.description: The branch checked out in `cwd`, as the host last reported it.

git_dirty.description: Whether `cwd`'s work tree had changes, as the host last reported.

hat_id.description:
The hat the session belongs to (umbrella §8.2), decided at its
start: a hat's id, or empty for a session from before hats whose
host and owner had no default hat to give it.

last_event_at.description:
When its last listed event was written (RFC 3339, UTC, three
fractional digits): the list's sort key, newest first.

model.description: The current model and mode, as the host last reported them.

presumed_parked.description:
Parked only because its host has been offline past the threshold
(ACP core §5.3); the host may still be running it.

title.description: The title the agent reported, on one line and capped.

SessionPage.description:
`GET /api/sessions` (ACP core §9): one page of the session list, newest
`last_event_at` first.

next_cursor.description:
Where the next page starts, for `cursor` (opaque); absent on the last
page.

SettingsResponse.description: `GET /api/settings` (kernel spec §8), and the answer to its `PATCH`.

contact.description:
The owner's push contact (kernel spec §6): an e-mail address the
push services may write to. Absent: they are given an `https`
`public_url`, and nothing for an `http` one, which Apple refuses.

SettingsUpdateRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/settings`: absent fields stay as they are. `contact` is an
e-mail address, trimmed, or empty (or blank) to clear it. `public_url` is not changed here
yet: `hennery admin reset-public-url` does that (kernel spec §4.2).

SetupRequest.description:
`POST /api/setup` (kernel spec §3.1): the one-time owner setup, with the
token from the setup link. `Debug` leaves the password out.

default_hat_name.description:
The default hat's name (kernel spec §3.1), 1 to 64 printable
characters. Absent: it stays "Personal".

public_url.description: `https://…`, or `http://` to a loopback address; an origin only.

SetupResponse.description:
201 to a setup: the owner is created and signed in (the session cookie
is set), and `public_url` is stored as this origin.

StartSessionRequest.description: `POST /api/sessions` (ACP core §9): `{host_id, agent, cwd, model?, mode?, axes?}`.

StepUpRequest.description:
`POST /api/auth/step-up/password` (kernel spec §3.4): the owner's
password again, within a session. 204 on success. `Debug` leaves the
password out.

StoredBlock.description:
One block of a prompt as the collector stores it (ACP core §7, plan 6a):
in `turns.content` and in the `user_turn` event's `content`. Text as it
was sent; an image as the attachment it was stored as, never its bytes.
`GET /api/attachments/{sha256}` serves the image.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the image's bytes, 64 lowercase hex digits.

size.description: The image's size in bytes, decoded.

TranscriptRemoval.description:
The agent's own transcript of a deleted session on its host (plan 9d
decision 7): best effort. `notes` name what is never removed, whatever
the state.

TurnOutcome.description: How a turn ended. Exactly one `turn_ended` per accepted turn (ACP core §4.4).

UpdateHatRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/hats/{id}`: absent fields stay as they are.
`default_for_new_hosts` can only be `true`: a hat stops being that
default when another takes its place.

UpdateHostRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/hosts/{id}` (kernel spec §4.3, §8): rename a host, or change
its default hat. Absent fields stay as they are.

UpdateMcpConnectionRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/mcp/connections/{id}`: 200 with the `McpConnectionItem` as
it is now. An absent field keeps its value; a `null` allowlist clears it
(every tool), `""` clears the prefix (gateway spec §4.6); a `null` for
another field reads as absent. Naming `url`, `cred_kind`,
`internal_network`, `static_header` or `static_prefix` needs step-up,
even with its stored value. Another origin (scheme, host, port) or
another kind deletes the stored credential and starts the status over
at `not_connected`, in the same change. The slug and the hat cannot
change: naming them is an unknown field.

Its own codes, beyond every route's (see `McpConnectionItem`): 403
`step_up_required`; 404 `not_found`; 400 `invalid` (`message` says
which field); 400 `unsupported_cred_kind`. A refused change changes
nothing.

cred_kind.description: Step-up. Another kind deletes the credential.

internal_network.description: Step-up. `false` is refused while the URL is `http`.

label.description:
1 to 64 bytes of UTF-8 once trimmed (stored trimmed), with no
control or invisible format character.

static_header.description: Step-up. As on create; cannot be empty.

static_prefix.description: Step-up. As on create; `""` clears it.

tool_allowlist.description:
Absent: kept. `null`: cleared (every tool). A list: set, as on
create.

url.description: Step-up. As on create; another origin deletes the credential.

UpdateSessionRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` (ACP core §9): absent fields stay as they are.
`hat_id` re-assigns the session (ACP core §4.9): only with no running
adapter, and with a fresh step-up.

VapidKeyResponse.description:
`GET /api/push/vapid` (kernel spec §6): the collector's VAPID public key,
the uncompressed P-256 point in base64url, which a browser's
`pushManager.subscribe` takes as `applicationServerKey`.
